name: Schloss Tratzberg
kurzbeschreibung: Stately Renaissance castle perched above the Inn Valley featuring original state rooms, historic armouries, and award-winning audio drama tours.
preis: Erwachsene ca. 15,00 €, Kinder ca. 9,00 €, inklusive Hörspielführung
beschreibung:
Overview

The majestic Schloss Tratzberg commands sweeping views across the lower Inn Valley from its forested ridge between Jenbach and Stans. Originally mentioned in the 13th century as a border stronghold against Bavaria, the medieval castle burned down in 1492. Emperor Maximilian I transferred the ruin to wealthy Schwaz mining magnates, the Tänzl brothers, who transformed it into an exquisite late Gothic and early Renaissance jewel. Owned by the Counts of Enzenberg since 1848, the castle remains one of the best-preserved and most authentically furnished Renaissance fortresses in the Alps.

Route & Requirements

From the car park in the valley, visitors can either take a scenic 20-minute uphill woodland stroll or ride the cheerful "Tratzberg-Express" fun train to the castle gates. Interior tours take approximately one hour and utilize an immersive wireless audio-play guide, where historical figures such as Emperor Maximilian I narrate their lives. Highlights include the arcaded courtyard, the Habsburg Hall with its monumental 46-metre painted genealogical tree, the Queen's Chamber with intricate woodwork, and the Armoury. A dedicated fairy-tale audio guide is provided for children with ghost Tratzi.

Visit & Arrival

Schloss Tratzberg welcomes visitors daily from early April until early November, operating from 10:00 to 16:00. Standard admission including the audio tour is roughly 15.00 Euro for adults and 9.00 Euro for children. By car, take the Inntal motorway A12 to the Jenbach or Schwaz exits and follow signs to the castle parking area at the Schlosswirt tavern. Rail passengers arrive at Jenbach station, from where local buses operate, or walk to the castle base in about 25 minutes.

Tips

Enjoy lunch or refreshments in the beer garden of the Schlosswirt inn near the lower car park. You can combine your visit with a thrilling hike through the nearby Wolfsklamm gorge in Stans up to the historic pilgrimage monastery of St. Georgenberg.
